title: Whether a provider call follows a redirect off its configured origin, in three languages
pins: Whether a provider endpoint that answers with a redirect to a different scheme, host or port gets the request re-sent there. Provider requests carry the API key in a header, and HTTP clients disagree about which headers survive a cross-origin hop: Guzzle and fetch drop Authorization and keep x-api-key, urllib keeps both. A consumer who configured one endpoint has its key delivered to a server it never named, and nothing errors to say so. The rule pinned here does not depend on header names: a redirect that leaves the configured origin is not followed at all.
scope: The openai, anthropic and mistral providers, entered through Prism.text().using() with url and key from the environment, over each language's default transport and real loopback sockets. 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 to another host, the same host on another port, a protocol-relative Location and a scheme change, plus same-origin controls, the same-origin hop limit (a loop, and a chain of exactly five) and a same-origin Location carrying userinfo. NOT covered: streaming, embeddings and the other capabilities (each language's own regression tests cover them), the reference's other fifteen providers, per-call urls (per-call-url-guard refuses private ones before any request), a redirect chain that leaves and returns, and the error each SDK raises, which is outside the contract. Same-origin 307 and 308 on a POST are deliberately absent: Python's urllib does not follow those at all, so they measure a client limit rather than this rule.
construction: tools/cross-origin-redirect.mjs gives every row three raw TCP loopback servers (the configured endpoint, another host, and the endpoint's host on another port) and reads the observation off them, never off the SDK. The endpoint answers its first request with the row's redirect and everything else with 500. Native PHP runs Prism::text()->using() over Laravel's real HTTP client with a global middleware refusing any non-127.x host; native TypeScript runs Prism.text().using() over the real fetch, wrapped to refuse any non-127.x url; native Python runs Prism.text().using() over the default transport with DNS and connections refused for anything but a 127.x literal. tools/cross-origin-redirect/contract.mjs refuses any observation field but the three, a credential seen elsewhere without anything reaching elsewhere, and a row whose call never reached its endpoint.
findings: 72 of the first 72 rows agree against the default branches of prism, prism-ts and prism-py: in all 60 hostile rows the endpoint received exactly one request and no other origin received a connection or a byte of the key. Against the code before the same-origin fixes the suite discriminates: PHP and TypeScript followed all 60 hostile redirects, and the Anthropic x-api-key reached the other origin in 15 of them; Python followed 36 (urllib does not follow a 307 or 308 on a POST) and sent the key, Authorization included, in 27 across all three providers. Agreement here is a conclusion about behaviour, not about safety: the three fixes were written to one rule the same day, so a shared misreading of an origin would agree too. One divergence is outside this rule and recorded rather than hidden: a same-origin 307 or 308 on a POST is followed by PHP and TypeScript and not by Python. Corpus 0.1.37 adds nine rows. The hop limit (cor-0073..cor-0080): the reference follows five same-origin redirects and refuses the sixth, so a loop reaches the endpoint six times; the ports capped at ten and made eleven requests until the fix that moved them to five, and the loop rows discriminate that. A chain of exactly five is followed by all three. A same-origin Location carrying userinfo (cor-0075, cor-0078, cor-0081) does NOT agree, deliberately: the reference follows it (two requests reach the endpoint), and both ports refuse it with redirect_refused before a second request. The reference is frozen for this change, so the disagreement is recorded rather than aligned away; nothing reaches another origin in any language.

discrimination.gap: No mutation probe is delivered for this suite. The code before the fix fails 60 of 72 rows in PHP and TypeScript and 36 in Python, which serves as a coarse negative control.

php.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with php --check. PRISM_PHP_SRC points it at a prism checkout (CI uses the default branch); without it, it reads the installed reference in runners/php.

ts.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with ts --check; it reads the built sibling prism-ts/dist, or PRISM_TS_DIST.

py.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with py --check; it imports the installed package, or PRISM_PY_SRC.
